Wave A — Presence & Roster: the listener becomes visible

items: Personal Dev Fleet epic · Wave A

content.value: The fleet works but is invisible: listeners execute the four-verb contract live (Claude AND Codex, merged #5178), yet nothing anywhere can answer "who is listening right now, where, with what capacity?" This wave closes the one native gap the build plan names: a listener presence record, a heartbeat, and bp fleet roster — readable by the console — proven by killing a listener and watching it flip OFFLINE exactly at TTL, not before.
A listener is just a document. A heartbeat is just a pulse. The roster is just a read. Four verbs, no new concepts — presence is the four verbs given a place to stand.

blocks.text: The wish (verbatim)

content.value: "What we want is a simple system that makes the different dev servers be able to listen and interact with orchestrator - the simplest and easiest the better - also we want a dev fleet system which is extendable - as said earlier - it is kinda personal + should be able to sync to many datasets and be some kinda main spot for developers to work. Re-center done; now we got to start looping epic cycles on this until finished. This cycle: Wave A — presence & roster (the one native gap): a listener presence record + heartbeat in the listener skill/runner + bp fleet roster (terminal) readable by the console, with the kill-a-listener → OFFLINE-at-TTL proof. Honor the simplicity law: four verbs, no new concepts."

blocks.text: Ground truth at Strategize (2026-07-22)

items.value: Charter .claude/workflows/bp-personal-dev-fleet-charter.md carries PDF-D1..D15; epic task personal-dev-fleet-epic published (0 children yet — this is the epic's FIRST bp-epic-cycle wave). Wave A is first on the charter roadmap; acceptance criterion 0 of the epic IS this wave's proof.

Proven base verified on disk: .claude/skills/fleet-listener/SKILL.md + fleet-orchestrator (helpers/route.py 8/8, file-order.sh) + tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh (provider-neutral runner: claude|codex|custom, in-turn law encoded) + fleet-protocol.md.

The listener skill ALREADY anticipates this wave: §1 says 'Use the native roster mechanism if present (bp fleet …); until that ships, upsert a small presence record'. The runner does NOT register presence at all, and its listen loop POLLS bp task ready every 6s rather than using bp listen SSE.

Strong precedent found: Barkpark.Tasks.Pulse (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/pulse.ex) — the task-lease heartbeat. Its laws transfer wholesale: ts stamped SERVER-side; staleness computed AT READ (a pulse past TTL must READ stale, never lie fresh); atomic single-write renewal. There is also a Tasks.TtlSweeper (lease reaping) and — naming hazard — a completely separate Barkpark.Pulse (Shared Storm's anonymous public channels, plugins/pulse) that is NOT presence.

The plugin seam is clean: Barkpark.Plugins.Tasks registers schemas (register_schemas → Tasks.schema_definitions), owns its routes (register_routes → /v1/tasks/*), and feeds the manifest-driven bp CLI (cli_commands, ~12 verbs). A listener record + roster read + bp fleet verbs can ride this exact seam.

Scope is intrinsic (PDF-D2): a listener lives in the workspace/project/dataset that bp use set; the roster is scope-local. The 'personal main syncs MANY datasets' vision implies roster-per-scope now, aggregation later.
Known-bug fence lifecycle (task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects) is Wave D's; nothing in presence may depend on claim resources.

blocks.text: Direction — presence is a citizen of the ledger

content.value: The finished experience: you type bp fleet roster and see your personal fleet the way kubectl shows nodes — WORKER · AGENT · SCOPE · STATUS · CAPACITY · LAST SEEN · TTL — and you TRUST it, because staleness fails closed: a listener that stopped pulsing reads OFFLINE the moment its own TTL lapses, computed at read time from a server-stamped timestamp, with no reaper and no background job to drift. The orchestrator skill reads the same roster before dispatching; the console reads the same endpoint and shows the same truth. Kill a listener mid-idle and the roster flips it OFFLINE at TTL — not before, not by magic, not never.

The design is one sentence long: a listener is just a document, a heartbeat is just a pulse, the roster is just a read. Concretely (tentative — Decide finalizes): (1) a listener document type registered by the tasks plugin — worker-keyed id, status, agent kind, scope, declared capacity, server-stamped last_seen, SELF-DECLARED ttl; (2) a heartbeat write that reuses the pulse verb semantically (bp fleet pulse or equivalent — the fourth verb aimed at your own presence, never a fifth verb) on a lean write path that does not mint a revision per beat; (3) GET /v1/fleet/roster (tasks-plugin-owned route) computing status at read time — OFFLINE past each row's OWN ttl — consumed identically by bp fleet roster (terminal table) and the console (thin JSON readout; per PDF-D11 no fleet screen beyond prototype this wave); (4) the runner heartbeats in its listen loop (same process — dies with the worker), the resident skill registers on start and pulses at transitions with an honestly LONGER self-declared ttl; (5) an executable kill-a-listener proof harness that can FAIL: two listeners up, kill one, the survivor stays ONLINE, the corpse flips OFFLINE exactly at its TTL — mutation-tested so a roster that hardcodes ONLINE reds the proof.

The self-declared TTL is the keystone honesty move. A bash runner can beat every 30s cheaply → tight TTL, crisp OFFLINE. A resident Claude session idling on SSE CANNOT beat without burning a turn → it declares a longer TTL and the roster stays honest about what it knows. One rule (offline past YOUR OWN ttl) absorbs every listener form — no per-form special cases, and a heartbeat sidecar that outlives its dead session (which would LIE online) is banned: the heartbeat source must share fate with the worker.

blocks.text: Direction debate — three rivals, one winner

items.value: RIVAL A — DERIVED PRESENCE, NO RECORD: infer the roster from recent claim/pulse/close events already on the ledger; zero new writes, zero new types. REJECTED as primary: an idle listener that has never claimed is INVISIBLE — precisely the listener the orchestrator most needs to see; capacity and scope have no home; the kill-proof is unrunnable for an idle worker. Kept as an enrichment: the roster MAY cross-check presence against last task activity ('says idle, closed an order 40s ago').

RIVAL B — CONNECTION-BASED PRESENCE: bp listen already holds a persistent SSE connection; let the server treat connectedness as liveness (Phoenix.Presence-style) — disconnect = instantly offline, no heartbeat writes at all. Genuinely elegant, and it beats TTL on detection latency. REJECTED: it conflates 'holds a socket' with 'alive and able to work' (the runner today POLLS and holds no socket; Codex/custom adapters may never hold one); it welds presence to one transport, breaking provider-neutrality (PDF-D5); connection state is a NEW concept (channel/ETS presence) that dies on server restart; and the user-ratified wish explicitly names heartbeat + TTL. Kept as a future enrichment: the roster could later annotate 'feed: connected'.

RIVAL C (WINNER) — LEDGER-NATIVE RECORD: a listener document + pulse-shaped heartbeat + read-time TTL roster. Wins because it is the only candidate that is simultaneously (a) doctrine-pure — the ledger stays the ONLY bus (PDF-D2), presence rides the same document machinery orders ride, zero new infrastructure; (b) form-neutral — skill sessions, bash runners, Codex, future cloud supports all write the same record; (c) fail-closed by construction (PDF-D6) — OFFLINE is computed from absence of evidence, so every crash mode converges to the truth; (d) already the codebase's own law — Tasks.Pulse encodes server-stamped ts + staleness-computed-at-read; we extend a proven idiom rather than invent one.

SHARPEST ATTACK on the winner: heartbeat writes through the full document pipeline could be a slow poison — a beat every 30-60s per listener minting revisions, firing lifecycle hooks, possibly GitHub-syncing (tasks sync to issues!) → history bloat and write amplification that only shows up after a week of honest use, exactly the 'leave it running for a week' bar the build plan sets. ABSORPTION: (1) the heartbeat gets a LEAN write path — a small plugin-owned endpoint that upserts last_seen/status without minting a revision per beat (Tasks.Pulse already proves the single-atomic-update idiom for exactly this reason); (2) the listener type is explicitly excluded from GitHub sync and from any hook not needed; (3) the survey MEASURES the cost (does a doc patch mint a revision? what do hooks fire on?) before Decide commits the write path; (4) TTLs are minutes not seconds — presence for a personal fleet of ~2-10 workers, not a datacenter — so worst-case write volume is trivially small even naive.

SECOND ATTACK: 'no new concepts' vs a new document type. RESOLUTION: the simplicity law bans a fifth VERB, a second BUS, and concepts the four-verb core does not need. Presence IS needed by the core (PDF-D6 is charter law; the orchestrator cannot route on min(declared, observed) without it), and 'an order is just a task' generalizes to 'a listener is just a document' — the same move that made orders cheap makes presence cheap. A record type is vocabulary, not protocol.

blocks.text: Key choices (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

items.value: Record: listener document type, worker-name-keyed, registered via the tasks plugin's register_schemas seam. Fields: worker, status (idle|working|blocked — drawn from the gui-plan 7-state catalogue, with offline always COMPUTED never stored), agent kind, scope, capacity envelope, last_seen (SERVER-stamped, never client-supplied — clock skew must not exist), ttl_seconds (self-declared).

Heartbeat: pulse-shaped, lean single-atomic-write, no revision minting, no GitHub sync, shares fate with the worker process (runner beats in-loop; skill beats at start/claim/close transitions with a longer declared ttl). Verb naming stays inside the four-verb vocabulary.

Roster: ONE server read computes status (fail-closed at each row's own TTL); bp fleet roster renders it in the terminal; the console consumes the SAME endpoint. No reaper process — absence of pulse IS the offline signal. Roster enriched with last task activity where cheap.

Skill + runner updated in-wave: fleet-run.sh registers + beats (and this wave is the natural moment to decide whether its listen loop adopts bp listen SSE or stays polling — survey will say); fleet-listener SKILL.md's 'until that ships' clause is REPLACED by the native mechanism; fleet-orchestrator reads the roster before dispatch.

Proof: executable harness (PDS proof-harness precedent) — two listeners, kill one, OFFLINE exactly at TTL, survivor unaffected; mutation-tested per the make-the-check-able-to-fail law. The epic's criterion-0 evidence comes from this proof's run output.

Console this wave = readable, not designed: a thin authenticated JSON consumption path (and at most a prototype readout), honoring PDF-D11's 'data before pixels'. The Fleet Card and 7-state screens come after the roster exists.

blocks.text: Survey digest — 15/15 lanes returned (2026-07-22)

content.value: THE DIRECTION SURVIVES CONTACT. Every lane confirms the ledger-native record. The seam is real: bp fleet roster needs ZERO Go for dispatch — internal/manifest/tree.go builds noun/verb nodes purely from the manifest (zero hardcoded nouns), plugin route tuples are LITERAL full paths (a /fleet/roster tuple mounts at GET /v1/fleet/roster), and no /v1/fleet route or fleet CLI noun exists anywhere (clean namespace). register_schemas/1 returns a list — adding listener_schema is a one-line edit plus a schema builder; plugin.json's nouns array needs "fleet" appended or provenance silently degrades to the generic tag. GitHub sync structurally excludes any non-task type (Outbox.fetch hardcodes e.type == "task" as a SQL literal, sole event source for the drain) — the beats-open-issues disaster is impossible UNLESS a builder registers listeners under type "task"; that becomes an explicit acceptance criterion, not a hope. The fence-lifecycle bug is Wave D and presence never touches --resources — zero coupling, confirmed in both skills and the runner.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK LANDED — AND WAS MEASURED. Heartbeats through the plain document path are the slow poison the debate predicted: every Content.upsert_document patch unconditionally inserts 3 rows (full-content revision snapshot + mutation_event + audit) with NO revision GC anywhere — 43k-86k rows/day for a 10-listener fleet at 30s beats, a third of it permanent revision noise. The lean Tasks.Pulse idiom (raw atomic Repo.update_all bypassing Content entirely) mints ZERO revision/audit rows and exactly 1 mutation_event. The charter's lean-write clause is therefore mandatory. Two refinements Decide must pin: (a) Tasks.Pulse is a PATTERN, not a callable — its check_holder gate is claim-lease-specific and would always refuse a listener; the wave needs a sibling module with its own advisory-lock family (listener:<doc_id>), a worker-identity gate, and server-stamped last_seen (all 10 task write modules already stamp DateTime.utc_now() server-side — client clocks never trusted). (b) 'Mints no revision per beat' means no revision ROW; the doc's rev field still bumps (no non-content column exists on documents). Whether even the 1 mutation_event per beat is needed is OPEN — the roster is a pure read with no SSE-tick consumer named; a verifier now enumerates every mutation_events consumer to answer it.

CONTRADICTIONS RESOLVED OR FLAGGED. (i) fleet-orchestrator SKILL.md §6 names Herd report_state as this mechanism's 'native home' — charter PDF-D12 overrules (herd demoted to optional-later; canonical roster = Fleet Card + bp fleet roster; herd-s6 is still an unbuilt open task, so no live migration conflict) and the SKILL.md line gets amended in-wave. (ii) Shared Storm's Barkpark.Pulse doctrine ('presence rows are ephemeral ROWS, not documents — draft logic and webhook fan-out are pure overhead') cuts against 'a listener is just a document'; the lean write path answers the same concern, but Decide must say so explicitly rather than silently disagree with adjacent prior art. (iii) Naming: this wave adds the repo's FOURTH 'fleet' (cloud instance fleet, chat FleetHub, epic_fleet.ex) and fourth 'pulse/presence' — new moduledocs must self-disambiguate exactly the way Tasks.Pulse's own moduledoc already does. (iv) PDF-D2's 'scope is intrinsic via bp use' is only HALF-true: flat token_root mutation routes derive tenancy from the BEARER TOKEN (DeriveWorkspaceFromToken → AssignDefaultScope fallback), not from local bp use config; only the scoped read family threads bp-use context. The heartbeat write and the roster read MUST ride the same scope source or the roster silently reads empty — a verifier settles the mount.

THE ONE HIDDEN GO TRAP IS RENDERING, NOT DISPATCH. renderTable only unwraps list payloads whose envelope key sits on a hardcoded Go allowlist (documents, docs, hits, …). A bespoke {"roster": [...]} envelope degrades to one crammed key/value cell on EVERY installed bp binary until a Go edit + fresh cli-v* release + reinstall propagates — directly undermining 'works on a stranger's machine instantly'. Cheapest honest path: the roster response nests rows under the already-allowlisted documents key (zero Go). Kubectl-style WORKER-first column order needs a cosmetic pickColumns edit; Decide rules whether that is in-wave Go or backlog polish. install-cli.sh's old 404 is fixed and closed — a stranger's first install works today.

FATE-SHARING IS SETTLED AND THE PROOF CAN RUN LOCALLY. PDS-D243/D263 already paid for the sidecar lesson: '& disown' children die or survive depending on WHICH signal kills the parent (ambiguous), and setsid detach is structurally immortal — so the detached-heartbeat ban holds with receipts. The bash runner beats INSIDE its single foreground loop (it currently has NO idle beat at all — pulse only fires mid-order; adding that beat is the wave's runner change, and the single-process shape must be called out as load-bearing, not incidental). The resident skill beats only at turn boundaries (idle-costs-nothing law: an SSE-parked session cannot beat) → honestly longer TTL; NO numeric TTL precedent exists anywhere in Barkpark — Decide picks fresh numbers per form. The kill-a-listener proof runs locally: the mix phx.server OOM does NOT apply to the compiled-release path — scripts/pds-scratch-target.sh boots an isolated instance (own PG + HTTP port, token minted) in ~10-33s WARM, and PDS's negative-control flags are the exact mutation-test pattern (stub status to always-online, assert the harness REDS). Roster status must be computed server-side in ONE module — the repo already carries 3 drifted copies of the same staleness math across two languages — and 'working on task-X' must be a read-time join on claim.worker || assignee (board_live.ex:1013), never a stored status string (lease expiry keeps assignee but frees the claim — a stored copy would lie).

OPERATIONAL HAZARD, PRE-EXISTING BUT BLOCKING: this checkout's main is 8 commits ahead / 136 behind origin/main, and the epic charter file (.claude/workflows/bp-personal-dev-fleet-charter.md) exists ONLY locally — it is not on origin/main. tooling/fleet/ and both fleet skills ARE on origin/main (merged #5178, byte-identical). Builders must work in worktrees cut from origin/main, and the charter must land via a clean PR, or the epic's constitution stays invisible to every other session. A verifier confirms the exact state and hands Decide a steward plan.

blocks.text: Verification — what the deep round proved (2026-07-22)

content.value: WRITE-COST KEYSTONE PROVEN AT L1 (scratch-live-writecost). On a live scratch release (booted 14.4s warm via pds-scratch-target.sh): two pulses moved revisions 5→5, audit 5→5, mutation_events 6→8 (both new events exactly task.pulse) — the lean idiom is 0 revision / 0 audit / 1 event per beat. Two plain content writes moved revisions 2→4, events 2→4, audit 2→4 — 3 rows per plain write, as the digest predicted. Caveats inherited by the proof harness: bp task verbs 403 on a bare-token scratch server (flat routes + bearer token work — the harness must curl flat routes), and the Sanity-style patch envelope 400'd on that build (createOrReplace was the measured plain write).

ZERO-GO RENDERING PROVEN AT RUNTIME (cli-envelope-proof). A {"documents":[roster-row]} payload renders a real multi-column table (probe test output quoted in the report); a bespoke {"roster":[...]} key degrades to ONE crammed KV cell and also breaks extractListRows pagination. pickColumns will NOT lead with WORKER (status leads, worker sorts last) — WORKER-first is a cosmetic Go backlog item. Live corroboration: bp task ls -o json against production returns {"docs":[...]} and renders a real table today. NOT-FOUND: the assignment's charter path did not exist in git history anywhere — the epic brief's own pointer was stale (steward task fixes it). Orthogonal find: go test ./internal/cli hangs on macOS via a pre-existing captureExecuteCode pipe deadlock (ubuntu CI green) — filed pdf-bl-go-test-pipe-deadlock.

EVENT-CONSUMER CENSUS (mutation-events-consumers). insert_mutation_event! never reaches webhook dispatch (bare Repo.insert!; dispatch lives only in Content.Broadcast.tap_broadcast, which task-family writes never call). GitHub outbox, /v1/tasks/events and /v1/tasks/prime are all hard-scoped to type=="task" — safe iff listeners are NEVER task-typed. THE REAL LEAK: Sync.Outbox.fetch has NO type filter, and any non-"task."-prefixed mutation falls to push_doc = full createOrReplace to every push-enabled remote. Verdict adopted: a ZERO-new-row beat is possible and lower-risk (the roster reads last_seen off the doc; nothing needs beat events), plus a structural type!="listener" exclusion in Sync.Outbox for the remaining registration events. mutation_events is already 63k rows, unbounded, never purged — independent support for zero-row.

TENANCY RULING (tenancy-mount). Mount FLAT at /v1/fleet/* copying the task family exactly — which rides AssignDefaultScope (NOT DeriveWorkspaceFromToken; that plug lives only on cycle/media/search-admin pipelines — the digest's framing was half-wrong and is corrected). On a personal box multi_tenant? is false and dataset is the only live axis. The roster read copies Tasks.Board.snapshot: global-per-dataset, NO workspace clause — divergence structurally impossible; the workspace-filtered index shape would fail-close to EMPTY on a nil workspace. A socket-scoped (LiveScope) console read is forbidden; the console hits the same flat endpoint. The harness additionally asserts the survivor row is RETURNED (catches empty-read bugs the ONLINE assert would miss).

blocks.text: Direction — presence is a citizen of the ledger

content.value: The finished experience: you type bp fleet roster and see your personal fleet the way kubectl shows nodes — WORKER · AGENT · SCOPE · STATUS · CAPACITY · LAST SEEN · TTL — and you TRUST it, because staleness fails closed: a listener that stopped pulsing reads OFFLINE the moment its own TTL lapses, computed at read time from a server-stamped timestamp, with no reaper and no background job to drift. The orchestrator skill reads the same roster before dispatching; the console reads the same endpoint and shows the same truth. Kill a listener mid-idle and the roster flips it OFFLINE at TTL — not before, not by magic, not never.

The design is one sentence long: a listener is just a document, a heartbeat is just a pulse, the roster is just a read. Concretely (tentative — Decide finalizes): (1) a listener document type registered by the tasks plugin — worker-keyed id, status, agent kind, scope, declared capacity, server-stamped last_seen, SELF-DECLARED ttl; (2) a heartbeat write that reuses the pulse verb semantically (bp fleet pulse or equivalent — the fourth verb aimed at your own presence, never a fifth verb) on a lean write path that does not mint a revision per beat; (3) GET /v1/fleet/roster (tasks-plugin-owned route) computing status at read time — OFFLINE past each row's OWN ttl — consumed identically by bp fleet roster (terminal table) and the console (thin JSON readout; per PDF-D11 no fleet screen beyond prototype this wave); (4) the runner heartbeats in its listen loop (same process — dies with the worker), the resident skill registers on start and pulses at transitions with an honestly LONGER self-declared ttl; (5) an executable kill-a-listener proof harness that can FAIL: two listeners up, kill one, the survivor stays ONLINE, the corpse flips OFFLINE exactly at its TTL — mutation-tested so a roster that hardcodes ONLINE reds the proof.

The self-declared TTL is the keystone honesty move. A bash runner can beat every 30s cheaply → tight TTL, crisp OFFLINE. A resident Claude session idling on SSE CANNOT beat without burning a turn → it declares a longer TTL and the roster stays honest about what it knows. One rule (offline past YOUR OWN ttl) absorbs every listener form — no per-form special cases, and a heartbeat sidecar that outlives its dead session (which would LIE online) is banned: the heartbeat source must share fate with the worker.

blocks.text: Direction debate — three rivals, one winner

items.value: RIVAL A — DERIVED PRESENCE, NO RECORD: infer the roster from recent claim/pulse/close events already on the ledger; zero new writes, zero new types. REJECTED as primary: an idle listener that has never claimed is INVISIBLE — precisely the listener the orchestrator most needs to see; capacity and scope have no home; the kill-proof is unrunnable for an idle worker. Kept as an enrichment: the roster MAY cross-check presence against last task activity ('says idle, closed an order 40s ago').

RIVAL B — CONNECTION-BASED PRESENCE: bp listen already holds a persistent SSE connection; let the server treat connectedness as liveness (Phoenix.Presence-style) — disconnect = instantly offline, no heartbeat writes at all. Genuinely elegant, and it beats TTL on detection latency. REJECTED: it conflates 'holds a socket' with 'alive and able to work' (the runner today POLLS and holds no socket; Codex/custom adapters may never hold one); it welds presence to one transport, breaking provider-neutrality (PDF-D5); connection state is a NEW concept (channel/ETS presence) that dies on server restart; and the user-ratified wish explicitly names heartbeat + TTL. Kept as a future enrichment: the roster could later annotate 'feed: connected'.

RIVAL C (WINNER) — LEDGER-NATIVE RECORD: a listener document + pulse-shaped heartbeat + read-time TTL roster. Wins because it is the only candidate that is simultaneously (a) doctrine-pure — the ledger stays the ONLY bus (PDF-D2), presence rides the same document machinery orders ride, zero new infrastructure; (b) form-neutral — skill sessions, bash runners, Codex, future cloud supports all write the same record; (c) fail-closed by construction (PDF-D6) — OFFLINE is computed from absence of evidence, so every crash mode converges to the truth; (d) already the codebase's own law — Tasks.Pulse encodes server-stamped ts + staleness-computed-at-read; we extend a proven idiom rather than invent one.

SHARPEST ATTACK on the winner: heartbeat writes through the full document pipeline could be a slow poison — a beat every 30-60s per listener minting revisions, firing lifecycle hooks, possibly GitHub-syncing (tasks sync to issues!) → history bloat and write amplification that only shows up after a week of honest use, exactly the 'leave it running for a week' bar the build plan sets. ABSORPTION: (1) the heartbeat gets a LEAN write path — a small plugin-owned endpoint that upserts last_seen/status without minting a revision per beat (Tasks.Pulse already proves the single-atomic-update idiom for exactly this reason); (2) the listener type is explicitly excluded from GitHub sync and from any hook not needed; (3) the survey MEASURES the cost (does a doc patch mint a revision? what do hooks fire on?) before Decide commits the write path; (4) TTLs are minutes not seconds — presence for a personal fleet of ~2-10 workers, not a datacenter — so worst-case write volume is trivially small even naive.

SECOND ATTACK: 'no new concepts' vs a new document type. RESOLUTION: the simplicity law bans a fifth VERB, a second BUS, and concepts the four-verb core does not need. Presence IS needed by the core (PDF-D6 is charter law; the orchestrator cannot route on min(declared, observed) without it), and 'an order is just a task' generalizes to 'a listener is just a document' — the same move that made orders cheap makes presence cheap. A record type is vocabulary, not protocol.

blocks.text: Survey digest — 15/15 lanes returned (2026-07-22)

content.value: THE DIRECTION SURVIVES CONTACT. Every lane confirms the ledger-native record. The seam is real: bp fleet roster needs ZERO Go for dispatch — internal/manifest/tree.go builds noun/verb nodes purely from the manifest (zero hardcoded nouns), plugin route tuples are LITERAL full paths (a /fleet/roster tuple mounts at GET /v1/fleet/roster), and no /v1/fleet route or fleet CLI noun exists anywhere (clean namespace). register_schemas/1 returns a list — adding listener_schema is a one-line edit plus a schema builder; plugin.json's nouns array needs "fleet" appended or provenance silently degrades to the generic tag. GitHub sync structurally excludes any non-task type (Outbox.fetch hardcodes e.type == "task" as a SQL literal, sole event source for the drain) — the beats-open-issues disaster is impossible UNLESS a builder registers listeners under type "task"; that becomes an explicit acceptance criterion, not a hope. The fence-lifecycle bug is Wave D and presence never touches --resources — zero coupling, confirmed in both skills and the runner.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK LANDED — AND WAS MEASURED. Heartbeats through the plain document path are the slow poison the debate predicted: every Content.upsert_document patch unconditionally inserts 3 rows (full-content revision snapshot + mutation_event + audit) with NO revision GC anywhere — 43k-86k rows/day for a 10-listener fleet at 30s beats, a third of it permanent revision noise. The lean Tasks.Pulse idiom (raw atomic Repo.update_all bypassing Content entirely) mints ZERO revision/audit rows and exactly 1 mutation_event. The charter's lean-write clause is therefore mandatory. Two refinements Decide must pin: (a) Tasks.Pulse is a PATTERN, not a callable — its check_holder gate is claim-lease-specific and would always refuse a listener; the wave needs a sibling module with its own advisory-lock family (listener:<doc_id>), a worker-identity gate, and server-stamped last_seen (all 10 task write modules already stamp DateTime.utc_now() server-side — client clocks never trusted). (b) 'Mints no revision per beat' means no revision ROW; the doc's rev field still bumps (no non-content column exists on documents). Whether even the 1 mutation_event per beat is needed is OPEN — the roster is a pure read with no SSE-tick consumer named; a verifier now enumerates every mutation_events consumer to answer it.

CONTRADICTIONS RESOLVED OR FLAGGED. (i) fleet-orchestrator SKILL.md §6 names Herd report_state as this mechanism's 'native home' — charter PDF-D12 overrules (herd demoted to optional-later; canonical roster = Fleet Card + bp fleet roster; herd-s6 is still an unbuilt open task, so no live migration conflict) and the SKILL.md line gets amended in-wave. (ii) Shared Storm's Barkpark.Pulse doctrine ('presence rows are ephemeral ROWS, not documents — draft logic and webhook fan-out are pure overhead') cuts against 'a listener is just a document'; the lean write path answers the same concern, but Decide must say so explicitly rather than silently disagree with adjacent prior art. (iii) Naming: this wave adds the repo's FOURTH 'fleet' (cloud instance fleet, chat FleetHub, epic_fleet.ex) and fourth 'pulse/presence' — new moduledocs must self-disambiguate exactly the way Tasks.Pulse's own moduledoc already does. (iv) PDF-D2's 'scope is intrinsic via bp use' is only HALF-true: flat token_root mutation routes derive tenancy from the BEARER TOKEN (DeriveWorkspaceFromToken → AssignDefaultScope fallback), not from local bp use config; only the scoped read family threads bp-use context. The heartbeat write and the roster read MUST ride the same scope source or the roster silently reads empty — a verifier settles the mount.

THE ONE HIDDEN GO TRAP IS RENDERING, NOT DISPATCH. renderTable only unwraps list payloads whose envelope key sits on a hardcoded Go allowlist (documents, docs, hits, …). A bespoke {"roster": [...]} envelope degrades to one crammed key/value cell on EVERY installed bp binary until a Go edit + fresh cli-v* release + reinstall propagates — directly undermining 'works on a stranger's machine instantly'. Cheapest honest path: the roster response nests rows under the already-allowlisted documents key (zero Go). Kubectl-style WORKER-first column order needs a cosmetic pickColumns edit; Decide rules whether that is in-wave Go or backlog polish. install-cli.sh's old 404 is fixed and closed — a stranger's first install works today.

FATE-SHARING IS SETTLED AND THE PROOF CAN RUN LOCALLY. PDS-D243/D263 already paid for the sidecar lesson: '& disown' children die or survive depending on WHICH signal kills the parent (ambiguous), and setsid detach is structurally immortal — so the detached-heartbeat ban holds with receipts. The bash runner beats INSIDE its single foreground loop (it currently has NO idle beat at all — pulse only fires mid-order; adding that beat is the wave's runner change, and the single-process shape must be called out as load-bearing, not incidental). The resident skill beats only at turn boundaries (idle-costs-nothing law: an SSE-parked session cannot beat) → honestly longer TTL; NO numeric TTL precedent exists anywhere in Barkpark — Decide picks fresh numbers per form. The kill-a-listener proof runs locally: the mix phx.server OOM does NOT apply to the compiled-release path — scripts/pds-scratch-target.sh boots an isolated instance (own PG + HTTP port, token minted) in ~10-33s WARM, and PDS's negative-control flags are the exact mutation-test pattern (stub status to always-online, assert the harness REDS). body.html:
PERSONAL DEV FLEET · WAVE A · STRATEGY

Wave A — Presence & Roster: the listener becomes visible

Personal Dev Fleet epic · Wave A · Opened at Strategize · 2026-07-22

The fleet works but is invisible: listeners execute the four-verb contract live (Claude AND Codex, merged #5178), yet nothing anywhere can answer "who is listening right now, where, with what capacity?" This wave closes the one native gap the build plan names: a listener presence record, a heartbeat, and bp fleet roster — readable by the console — proven by killing a listener and watching it flip OFFLINE exactly at TTL, not before.

A listener is just a document. A heartbeat is just a pulse. The roster is just a read. Four verbs, no new concepts — presence is the four verbs given a place to stand.

The wish (verbatim)

"What we want is a simple system that makes the different dev servers be able to listen and interact with orchestrator - the simplest and easiest the better - also we want a dev fleet system which is extendable - as said earlier - it is kinda personal + should be able to sync to many datasets and be some kinda main spot for developers to work. Re-center done; now we got to start looping epic cycles on this until finished. This cycle: Wave A — presence & roster (the one native gap): a listener presence record + heartbeat in the listener skill/runner + bp fleet roster (terminal) readable by the console, with the kill-a-listener → OFFLINE-at-TTL proof. Honor the simplicity law: four verbs, no new concepts."

Ground truth at Strategize (2026-07-22)

• Charter .claude/workflows/bp-personal-dev-fleet-charter.md carries PDF-D1..D15; epic task personal-dev-fleet-epic published (0 children yet — this is the epic's FIRST bp-epic-cycle wave). Wave A is first on the charter roadmap; acceptance criterion 0 of the epic IS this wave's proof.
• Proven base verified on disk: .claude/skills/fleet-listener/SKILL.md + fleet-orchestrator (helpers/route.py 8/8, file-order.sh) + tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh (provider-neutral runner: claude|codex|custom, in-turn law encoded) + fleet-protocol.md.
• The listener skill ALREADY anticipates this wave: §1 says 'Use the native roster mechanism if present (bp fleet …); until that ships, upsert a small presence record'. The runner does NOT register presence at all, and its listen loop POLLS bp task ready every 6s rather than using bp listen SSE.
• Strong precedent found: Barkpark.Tasks.Pulse (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/pulse.ex) — the task-lease heartbeat. Its laws transfer wholesale: ts stamped SERVER-side; staleness computed AT READ (a pulse past TTL must READ stale, never lie fresh); atomic single-write renewal. There is also a Tasks.TtlSweeper (lease reaping) and — naming hazard — a completely separate Barkpark.Pulse (Shared Storm's anonymous public channels, plugins/pulse) that is NOT presence.
• The plugin seam is clean: Barkpark.Plugins.Tasks registers schemas (register_schemas → Tasks.schema_definitions), owns its routes (register_routes → /v1/tasks/*), and feeds the manifest-driven bp CLI (cli_commands, ~12 verbs). A listener record + roster read + bp fleet verbs can ride this exact seam.
• Scope is intrinsic (PDF-D2): a listener lives in the workspace/project/dataset that bp use set; the roster is scope-local. The 'personal main syncs MANY datasets' vision implies roster-per-scope now, aggregation later.
• Known-bug fence lifecycle (task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects) is Wave D's; nothing in presence may depend on claim resources.

Direction — presence is a citizen of the ledger

The finished experience: you type bp fleet roster and see your personal fleet the way kubectl shows nodes — WORKER · AGENT · SCOPE · STATUS · CAPACITY · LAST SEEN · TTL — and you TRUST it, because staleness fails closed: a listener that stopped pulsing reads OFFLINE the moment its own TTL lapses, computed at read time from a server-stamped timestamp, with no reaper and no background job to drift. The orchestrator skill reads the same roster before dispatching; the console reads the same endpoint and shows the same truth. Kill a listener mid-idle and the roster flips it OFFLINE at TTL — not before, not by magic, not never.

The design is one sentence long: a listener is just a document, a heartbeat is just a pulse, the roster is just a read. Concretely (tentative — Decide finalizes): (1) a listener document type registered by the tasks plugin — worker-keyed id, status, agent kind, scope, declared capacity, server-stamped last_seen, SELF-DECLARED ttl; (2) a heartbeat write that reuses the pulse verb semantically (bp fleet pulse or equivalent — the fourth verb aimed at your own presence, never a fifth verb) on a lean write path that does not mint a revision per beat; (3) GET /v1/fleet/roster (tasks-plugin-owned route) computing status at read time — OFFLINE past each row's OWN ttl — consumed identically by bp fleet roster (terminal table) and the console (thin JSON readout; per PDF-D11 no fleet screen beyond prototype this wave); (4) the runner heartbeats in its listen loop (same process — dies with the worker), the resident skill registers on start and pulses at transitions with an honestly LONGER self-declared ttl; (5) an executable kill-a-listener proof harness that can FAIL: two listeners up, kill one, the survivor stays ONLINE, the corpse flips OFFLINE exactly at its TTL — mutation-tested so a roster that hardcodes ONLINE reds the proof.

The self-declared TTL is the keystone honesty move. A bash runner can beat every 30s cheaply → tight TTL, crisp OFFLINE. A resident Claude session idling on SSE CANNOT beat without burning a turn → it declares a longer TTL and the roster stays honest about what it knows. One rule (offline past YOUR OWN ttl) absorbs every listener form — no per-form special cases, and a heartbeat sidecar that outlives its dead session (which would LIE online) is banned: the heartbeat source must share fate with the worker.

Direction debate — three rivals, one winner

• RIVAL A — DERIVED PRESENCE, NO RECORD: infer the roster from recent claim/pulse/close events already on the ledger; zero new writes, zero new types. REJECTED as primary: an idle listener that has never claimed is INVISIBLE — precisely the listener the orchestrator most needs to see; capacity and scope have no home; the kill-proof is unrunnable for an idle worker. Kept as an enrichment: the roster MAY cross-check presence against last task activity ('says idle, closed an order 40s ago').
• RIVAL B — CONNECTION-BASED PRESENCE: bp listen already holds a persistent SSE connection; let the server treat connectedness as liveness (Phoenix.Presence-style) — disconnect = instantly offline, no heartbeat writes at all. Genuinely elegant, and it beats TTL on detection latency. REJECTED: it conflates 'holds a socket' with 'alive and able to work' (the runner today POLLS and holds no socket; Codex/custom adapters may never hold one); it welds presence to one transport, breaking provider-neutrality (PDF-D5); connection state is a NEW concept (channel/ETS presence) that dies on server restart; and the user-ratified wish explicitly names heartbeat + TTL. Kept as a future enrichment: the roster could later annotate 'feed: connected'.
• RIVAL C (WINNER) — LEDGER-NATIVE RECORD: a listener document + pulse-shaped heartbeat + read-time TTL roster. Wins because it is the only candidate that is simultaneously (a) doctrine-pure — the ledger stays the ONLY bus (PDF-D2), presence rides the same document machinery orders ride, zero new infrastructure; (b) form-neutral — skill sessions, bash runners, Codex, future cloud supports all write the same record; (c) fail-closed by construction (PDF-D6) — OFFLINE is computed from absence of evidence, so every crash mode converges to the truth; (d) already the codebase's own law — Tasks.Pulse encodes server-stamped ts + staleness-computed-at-read; we extend a proven idiom rather than invent one.
• SHARPEST ATTACK on the winner: heartbeat writes through the full document pipeline could be a slow poison — a beat every 30-60s per listener minting revisions, firing lifecycle hooks, possibly GitHub-syncing (tasks sync to issues!) → history bloat and write amplification that only shows up after a week of honest use, exactly the 'leave it running for a week' bar the build plan sets. ABSORPTION: (1) the heartbeat gets a LEAN write path — a small plugin-owned endpoint that upserts last_seen/status without minting a revision per beat (Tasks.Pulse already proves the single-atomic-update idiom for exactly this reason); (2) the listener type is explicitly excluded from GitHub sync and from any hook not needed; (3) the survey MEASURES the cost (does a doc patch mint a revision? what do hooks fire on?) before Decide commits the write path; (4) TTLs are minutes not seconds — presence for a personal fleet of ~2-10 workers, not a datacenter — so worst-case write volume is trivially small even naive.
• SECOND ATTACK: 'no new concepts' vs a new document type. RESOLUTION: the simplicity law bans a fifth VERB, a second BUS, and concepts the four-verb core does not need. Presence IS needed by the core (PDF-D6 is charter law; the orchestrator cannot route on min(declared, observed) without it), and 'an order is just a task' generalizes to 'a listener is just a document' — the same move that made orders cheap makes presence cheap. A record type is vocabulary, not protocol.

Key choices (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

• Record: listener document type, worker-name-keyed, registered via the tasks plugin's register_schemas seam. Fields: worker, status (idle|working|blocked — drawn from the gui-plan 7-state catalogue, with offline always COMPUTED never stored), agent kind, scope, capacity envelope, last_seen (SERVER-stamped, never client-supplied — clock skew must not exist), ttl_seconds (self-declared).
• Heartbeat: pulse-shaped, lean single-atomic-write, no revision minting, no GitHub sync, shares fate with the worker process (runner beats in-loop; skill beats at start/claim/close transitions with a longer declared ttl). Verb naming stays inside the four-verb vocabulary.
• Roster: ONE server read computes status (fail-closed at each row's own TTL); bp fleet roster renders it in the terminal; the console consumes the SAME endpoint. No reaper process — absence of pulse IS the offline signal. Roster enriched with last task activity where cheap.
• Skill + runner updated in-wave: fleet-run.sh registers + beats (and this wave is the natural moment to decide whether its listen loop adopts bp listen SSE or stays polling — survey will say); fleet-listener SKILL.md's 'until that ships' clause is REPLACED by the native mechanism; fleet-orchestrator reads the roster before dispatch.
• Proof: executable harness (PDS proof-harness precedent) — two listeners, kill one, OFFLINE exactly at TTL, survivor unaffected; mutation-tested per the make-the-check-able-to-fail law. The epic's criterion-0 evidence comes from this proof's run output.
• Console this wave = readable, not designed: a thin authenticated JSON consumption path (and at most a prototype readout), honoring PDF-D11's 'data before pixels'. The Fleet Card and 7-state screens come after the roster exists.

Survey plan — 15 lanes, in flight

Fifteen Sonnet surveyors fly now: (1) tasks-plugin-seam — exactly what registering a listener type + roster route + a new bp fleet CLI verb group takes (can cli_commands mint a NEW top-level group?); (2) doc-write-cost — does a patch/upsert mint a revision per beat, which hooks fire, where a lean write path can live; (3) github-sync-scope — prove a listener type would NOT sync to GitHub issues; (4) pulse-anatomy — Tasks.Pulse's atomic-renewal idiom + TtlSweeper, what transfers verbatim; (5) sse-listen — how /v1/data/listen works, whether the server sees connections, why fleet-run.sh polls, whether the runner should adopt SSE this wave; (6) heartbeat-fate-sharing — for each listener form, where a beat can live so it DIES with the worker (Monitor wake semantics, background-child kill behavior), honest TTL per form; (7) cmux-prior-art — bp cmux claim/renew/close machinery worth mirroring; (8) herd-and-gui-prior-art — Herd Layer report_state shape (what must NOT be retrofitted per PDF-D12) + where the gui-plan specifies the Fleet Card and 7-state catalogue; (9) tenancy-scoping — how listener docs scope, what the per-scope roster query is, what many-datasets implies; (10) console-readability — what console surfaces exist (Studio desk/board, cloud console), the cheapest honest consumption path, auth tier; (11) ttl-computation — read-time computed-status precedents, single source of truth, server-stamp enforcement; (12) proof-harness — PDS/route.py proof precedents, where a kill-a-listener harness lives, whether it can run against local vs guerrilla, how it mutation-tests; (13) capabilities-manifest — how a new verb reaches users' bp binaries (manifest vs Go release, doctor freshness hook); (14) fence-and-frontier — confirm presence touches no claim resources; whether bp task frontier already exposes assignee data the roster should reuse; (15) collisions — open PRs, foreign claims, live sessions touching tasks plugin/CLI/fleet ground. Digest appends its distillation + the verify plan here BEFORE verifiers fly.

Survey digest — 15/15 lanes returned (2026-07-22)

THE DIRECTION SURVIVES CONTACT. Every lane confirms the ledger-native record. The seam is real: bp fleet roster needs ZERO Go for dispatch — internal/manifest/tree.go builds noun/verb nodes purely from the manifest (zero hardcoded nouns), plugin route tuples are LITERAL full paths (a /fleet/roster tuple mounts at GET /v1/fleet/roster), and no /v1/fleet route or fleet CLI noun exists anywhere (clean namespace). register_schemas/1 returns a list — adding listener_schema is a one-line edit plus a schema builder; plugin.json's nouns array needs "fleet" appended or provenance silently degrades to the generic tag. GitHub sync structurally excludes any non-task type (Outbox.fetch hardcodes e.type == "task" as a SQL literal, sole event source for the drain) — the beats-open-issues disaster is impossible UNLESS a builder registers listeners under type "task"; that becomes an explicit acceptance criterion, not a hope. The fence-lifecycle bug is Wave D and presence never touches --resources — zero coupling, confirmed in both skills and the runner.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK LANDED — AND WAS MEASURED. Heartbeats through the plain document path are the slow poison the debate predicted: every Content.upsert_document patch unconditionally inserts 3 rows (full-content revision snapshot + mutation_event + audit) with NO revision GC anywhere — 43k-86k rows/day for a 10-listener fleet at 30s beats, a third of it permanent revision noise. The lean Tasks.Pulse idiom (raw atomic Repo.update_all bypassing Content entirely) mints ZERO revision/audit rows and exactly 1 mutation_event. The charter's lean-write clause is therefore mandatory. Two refinements Decide must pin: (a) Tasks.Pulse is a PATTERN, not a callable — its check_holder gate is claim-lease-specific and would always refuse a listener; the wave needs a sibling module with its own advisory-lock family (listener:<doc_id>), a worker-identity gate, and server-stamped last_seen (all 10 task write modules already stamp DateTime.utc_now() server-side — client clocks never trusted). (b) 'Mints no revision per beat' means no revision ROW; the doc's rev field still bumps (no non-content column exists on documents). Whether even the 1 mutation_event per beat is needed is OPEN — the roster is a pure read with no SSE-tick consumer named; a verifier now enumerates every mutation_events consumer to answer it.

CONTRADICTIONS RESOLVED OR FLAGGED. (i) fleet-orchestrator SKILL.md §6 names Herd report_state as this mechanism's 'native home' — charter PDF-D12 overrules (herd demoted to optional-later; canonical roster = Fleet Card + bp fleet roster; herd-s6 is still an unbuilt open task, so no live migration conflict) and the SKILL.md line gets amended in-wave. (ii) Shared Storm's Barkpark.Pulse doctrine ('presence rows are ephemeral ROWS, not documents — draft logic and webhook fan-out are pure overhead') cuts against 'a listener is just a document'; the lean write path answers the same concern, but Decide must say so explicitly rather than silently disagree with adjacent prior art. (iii) Naming: this wave adds the repo's FOURTH 'fleet' (cloud instance fleet, chat FleetHub, epic_fleet.ex) and fourth 'pulse/presence' — new moduledocs must self-disambiguate exactly the way Tasks.Pulse's own moduledoc already does. (iv) PDF-D2's 'scope is intrinsic via bp use' is only HALF-true: flat token_root mutation routes derive tenancy from the BEARER TOKEN (DeriveWorkspaceFromToken → AssignDefaultScope fallback), not from local bp use config; only the scoped read family threads bp-use context. The heartbeat write and the roster read MUST ride the same scope source or the roster silently reads empty — a verifier settles the mount.

THE ONE HIDDEN GO TRAP IS RENDERING, NOT DISPATCH. renderTable only unwraps list payloads whose envelope key sits on a hardcoded Go allowlist (documents, docs, hits, …). A bespoke {"roster": [...]} envelope degrades to one crammed key/value cell on EVERY installed bp binary until a Go edit + fresh cli-v* release + reinstall propagates — directly undermining 'works on a stranger's machine instantly'. Cheapest honest path: the roster response nests rows under the already-allowlisted documents key (zero Go). Kubectl-style WORKER-first column order needs a cosmetic pickColumns edit; Decide rules whether that is in-wave Go or backlog polish. install-cli.sh's old 404 is fixed and closed — a stranger's first install works today.

FATE-SHARING IS SETTLED AND THE PROOF CAN RUN LOCALLY. PDS-D243/D263 already paid for the sidecar lesson: '& disown' children die or survive depending on WHICH signal kills the parent (ambiguous), and setsid detach is structurally immortal — so the detached-heartbeat ban holds with receipts. The bash runner beats INSIDE its single foreground loop (it currently has NO idle beat at all — pulse only fires mid-order; adding that beat is the wave's runner change, and the single-process shape must be called out as load-bearing, not incidental). PERSONAL DEV FLEET · WAVE A · STRATEGY

Wave A — Presence & Roster: the listener becomes visible

Personal Dev Fleet epic · Wave A · Opened at Strategize · 2026-07-22

The fleet works but is invisible: listeners execute the four-verb contract live (Claude AND Codex, merged #5178), yet nothing anywhere can answer "who is listening right now, where, with what capacity?" This wave closes the one native gap the build plan names: a listener presence record, a heartbeat, and bp fleet roster — readable by the console — proven by killing a listener and watching it flip OFFLINE exactly at TTL, not before.

A listener is just a document. A heartbeat is just a pulse. The roster is just a read. Four verbs, no new concepts — presence is the four verbs given a place to stand.

The wish (verbatim)

"What we want is a simple system that makes the different dev servers be able to listen and interact with orchestrator - the simplest and easiest the better - also we want a dev fleet system which is extendable - as said earlier - it is kinda personal + should be able to sync to many datasets and be some kinda main spot for developers to work. Re-center done; now we got to start looping epic cycles on this until finished. This cycle: Wave A — presence & roster (the one native gap): a listener presence record + heartbeat in the listener skill/runner + bp fleet roster (terminal) readable by the console, with the kill-a-listener → OFFLINE-at-TTL proof. Honor the simplicity law: four verbs, no new concepts."

Ground truth at Strategize (2026-07-22)

  • Charter .claude/workflows/bp-personal-dev-fleet-charter.md carries PDF-D1..D15; epic task personal-dev-fleet-epic published (0 children yet — this is the epic's FIRST bp-epic-cycle wave). Wave A is first on the charter roadmap; acceptance criterion 0 of the epic IS this wave's proof.
  • Proven base verified on disk: .claude/skills/fleet-listener/SKILL.md + fleet-orchestrator (helpers/route.py 8/8, file-order.sh) + tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh (provider-neutral runner: claude|codex|custom, in-turn law encoded) + fleet-protocol.md.
  • The listener skill ALREADY anticipates this wave: §1 says 'Use the native roster mechanism if present (bp fleet …); until that ships, upsert a small presence record'. The runner does NOT register presence at all, and its listen loop POLLS bp task ready every 6s rather than using bp listen SSE.
  • Strong precedent found: Barkpark.Tasks.Pulse (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/pulse.ex) — the task-lease heartbeat. Its laws transfer wholesale: ts stamped SERVER-side; staleness computed AT READ (a pulse past TTL must READ stale, never lie fresh); atomic single-write renewal. There is also a Tasks.TtlSweeper (lease reaping) and — naming hazard — a completely separate Barkpark.Pulse (Shared Storm's anonymous public channels, plugins/pulse) that is NOT presence.
  • The plugin seam is clean: Barkpark.Plugins.Tasks registers schemas (register_schemas → Tasks.schema_definitions), owns its routes (register_routes → /v1/tasks/*), and feeds the manifest-driven bp CLI (cli_commands, ~12 verbs). A listener record + roster read + bp fleet verbs can ride this exact seam.
  • Scope is intrinsic (PDF-D2): a listener lives in the workspace/project/dataset that bp use set; the roster is scope-local. The 'personal main syncs MANY datasets' vision implies roster-per-scope now, aggregation later.
  • Known-bug fence lifecycle (task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects) is Wave D's; nothing in presence may depend on claim resources.

Direction — presence is a citizen of the ledger

The finished experience: you type bp fleet roster and see your personal fleet the way kubectl shows nodes — WORKER · AGENT · SCOPE · STATUS · CAPACITY · LAST SEEN · TTL — and you TRUST it, because staleness fails closed: a listener that stopped pulsing reads OFFLINE the moment its own TTL lapses, computed at read time from a server-stamped timestamp, with no reaper and no background job to drift. The orchestrator skill reads the same roster before dispatching; the console reads the same endpoint and shows the same truth. Kill a listener mid-idle and the roster flips it OFFLINE at TTL — not before, not by magic, not never.

The design is one sentence long: a listener is just a document, a heartbeat is just a pulse, the roster is just a read. Concretely (tentative — Decide finalizes): (1) a listener document type registered by the tasks plugin — worker-keyed id, status, agent kind, scope, declared capacity, server-stamped last_seen, SELF-DECLARED ttl; (2) a heartbeat write that reuses the pulse verb semantically (bp fleet pulse or equivalent — the fourth verb aimed at your own presence, never a fifth verb) on a lean write path that does not mint a revision per beat; (3) GET /v1/fleet/roster (tasks-plugin-owned route) computing status at read time — OFFLINE past each row's OWN ttl — consumed identically by bp fleet roster (terminal table) and the console (thin JSON readout; per PDF-D11 no fleet screen beyond prototype this wave); (4) the runner heartbeats in its listen loop (same process — dies with the worker), the resident skill registers on start and pulses at transitions with an honestly LONGER self-declared ttl; (5) an executable kill-a-listener proof harness that can FAIL: two listeners up, kill one, the survivor stays ONLINE, the corpse flips OFFLINE exactly at its TTL — mutation-tested so a roster that hardcodes ONLINE reds the proof.

The self-declared TTL is the keystone honesty move. A bash runner can beat every 30s cheaply → tight TTL, crisp OFFLINE. A resident Claude session idling on SSE CANNOT beat without burning a turn → it declares a longer TTL and the roster stays honest about what it knows. One rule (offline past YOUR OWN ttl) absorbs every listener form — no per-form special cases, and a heartbeat sidecar that outlives its dead session (which would LIE online) is banned: the heartbeat source must share fate with the worker.

Direction debate — three rivals, one winner

  • RIVAL A — DERIVED PRESENCE, NO RECORD: infer the roster from recent claim/pulse/close events already on the ledger; zero new writes, zero new types. REJECTED as primary: an idle listener that has never claimed is INVISIBLE — precisely the listener the orchestrator most needs to see; capacity and scope have no home; the kill-proof is unrunnable for an idle worker. Kept as an enrichment: the roster MAY cross-check presence against last task activity ('says idle, closed an order 40s ago').
  • RIVAL B — CONNECTION-BASED PRESENCE: bp listen already holds a persistent SSE connection; let the server treat connectedness as liveness (Phoenix.Presence-style) — disconnect = instantly offline, no heartbeat writes at all. Genuinely elegant, and it beats TTL on detection latency. REJECTED: it conflates 'holds a socket' with 'alive and able to work' (the runner today POLLS and holds no socket; Codex/custom adapters may never hold one); it welds presence to one transport, breaking provider-neutrality (PDF-D5); connection state is a NEW concept (channel/ETS presence) that dies on server restart; and the user-ratified wish explicitly names heartbeat + TTL. Kept as a future enrichment: the roster could later annotate 'feed: connected'.
  • RIVAL C (WINNER) — LEDGER-NATIVE RECORD: a listener document + pulse-shaped heartbeat + read-time TTL roster. Wins because it is the only candidate that is simultaneously (a) doctrine-pure — the ledger stays the ONLY bus (PDF-D2), presence rides the same document machinery orders ride, zero new infrastructure; (b) form-neutral — skill sessions, bash runners, Codex, future cloud supports all write the same record; (c) fail-closed by construction (PDF-D6) — OFFLINE is computed from absence of evidence, so every crash mode converges to the truth; (d) already the codebase's own law — Tasks.Pulse encodes server-stamped ts + staleness-computed-at-read; we extend a proven idiom rather than invent one.
  • SHARPEST ATTACK on the winner: heartbeat writes through the full document pipeline could be a slow poison — a beat every 30-60s per listener minting revisions, firing lifecycle hooks, possibly GitHub-syncing (tasks sync to issues!) → history bloat and write amplification that only shows up after a week of honest use, exactly the 'leave it running for a week' bar the build plan sets. ABSORPTION: (1) the heartbeat gets a LEAN write path — a small plugin-owned endpoint that upserts last_seen/status without minting a revision per beat (Tasks.Pulse already proves the single-atomic-update idiom for exactly this reason); (2) the listener type is explicitly excluded from GitHub sync and from any hook not needed; (3) the survey MEASURES the cost (does a doc patch mint a revision? what do hooks fire on?) before Decide commits the write path; (4) TTLs are minutes not seconds — presence for a personal fleet of ~2-10 workers, not a datacenter — so worst-case write volume is trivially small even naive.
  • SECOND ATTACK: 'no new concepts' vs a new document type. RESOLUTION: the simplicity law bans a fifth VERB, a second BUS, and concepts the four-verb core does not need. Presence IS needed by the core (PDF-D6 is charter law; the orchestrator cannot route on min(declared, observed) without it), and 'an order is just a task' generalizes to 'a listener is just a document' — the same move that made orders cheap makes presence cheap. A record type is vocabulary, not protocol.

Key choices (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

  • Record: listener document type, worker-name-keyed, registered via the tasks plugin's register_schemas seam. Fields: worker, status (idle|working|blocked — drawn from the gui-plan 7-state catalogue, with offline always COMPUTED never stored), agent kind, scope, capacity envelope, last_seen (SERVER-stamped, never client-supplied — clock skew must not exist), ttl_seconds (self-declared).
  • Heartbeat: pulse-shaped, lean single-atomic-write, no revision minting, no GitHub sync, shares fate with the worker process (runner beats in-loop; skill beats at start/claim/close transitions with a longer declared ttl). Verb naming stays inside the four-verb vocabulary.
  • Roster: ONE server read computes status (fail-closed at each row's own TTL); bp fleet roster renders it in the terminal; the console consumes the SAME endpoint. No reaper process — absence of pulse IS the offline signal. Roster enriched with last task activity where cheap.
  • Skill + runner updated in-wave: fleet-run.sh registers + beats (and this wave is the natural moment to decide whether its listen loop adopts bp listen SSE or stays polling — survey will say); fleet-listener SKILL.md's 'until that ships' clause is REPLACED by the native mechanism; fleet-orchestrator reads the roster before dispatch.
  • Proof: executable harness (PDS proof-harness precedent) — two listeners, kill one, OFFLINE exactly at TTL, survivor unaffected; mutation-tested per the make-the-check-able-to-fail law. The epic's criterion-0 evidence comes from this proof's run output.
  • Console this wave = readable, not designed: a thin authenticated JSON consumption path (and at most a prototype readout), honoring PDF-D11's 'data before pixels'. The Fleet Card and 7-state screens come after the roster exists.

Survey plan — 15 lanes, in flight

Fifteen Sonnet surveyors fly now: (1) tasks-plugin-seam — exactly what registering a listener type + roster route + a new bp fleet CLI verb group takes (can cli_commands mint a NEW top-level group?); (2) doc-write-cost — does a patch/upsert mint a revision per beat, which hooks fire, where a lean write path can live; (3) github-sync-scope — prove a listener type would NOT sync to GitHub issues; (4) pulse-anatomy — Tasks.Pulse's atomic-renewal idiom + TtlSweeper, what transfers verbatim; (5) sse-listen — how /v1/data/listen works, whether the server sees connections, why fleet-run.sh polls, whether the runner should adopt SSE this wave; (6) heartbeat-fate-sharing — for each listener form, where a beat can live so it DIES with the worker (Monitor wake semantics, background-child kill behavior), honest TTL per form; (7) cmux-prior-art — bp cmux claim/renew/close machinery worth mirroring; (8) herd-and-gui-prior-art — Herd Layer report_state shape (what must NOT be retrofitted per PDF-D12) + where the gui-plan specifies the Fleet Card and 7-state catalogue; (9) tenancy-scoping — how listener docs scope, what the per-scope roster query is, what many-datasets implies; (10) console-readability — what console surfaces exist (Studio desk/board, cloud console), the cheapest honest consumption path, auth tier; (11) ttl-computation — read-time computed-status precedents, single source of truth, server-stamp enforcement; (12) proof-harness — PDS/route.py proof precedents, where a kill-a-listener harness lives, whether it can run against local vs guerrilla, how it mutation-tests; (13) capabilities-manifest — how a new verb reaches users' bp binaries (manifest vs Go release, doctor freshness hook); (14) fence-and-frontier — confirm presence touches no claim resources; whether bp task frontier already exposes assignee data the roster should reuse; (15) collisions — open PRs, foreign claims, live sessions touching tasks plugin/CLI/fleet ground. Digest appends its distillation + the verify plan here BEFORE verifiers fly.

Survey digest — 15/15 lanes returned (2026-07-22)

THE DIRECTION SURVIVES CONTACT. Every lane confirms the ledger-native record. The seam is real: bp fleet roster needs ZERO Go for dispatch — internal/manifest/tree.go builds noun/verb nodes purely from the manifest (zero hardcoded nouns), plugin route tuples are LITERAL full paths (a /fleet/roster tuple mounts at GET /v1/fleet/roster), and no /v1/fleet route or fleet CLI noun exists anywhere (clean namespace). register_schemas/1 returns a list — adding listener_schema is a one-line edit plus a schema builder; plugin.json's nouns array needs "fleet" appended or provenance silently degrades to the generic tag. GitHub sync structurally excludes any non-task type (Outbox.fetch hardcodes e.type == "task" as a SQL literal, sole event source for the drain) — the beats-open-issues disaster is impossible UNLESS a builder registers listeners under type "task"; that becomes an explicit acceptance criterion, not a hope. The fence-lifecycle bug is Wave D and presence never touches --resources — zero coupling, confirmed in both skills and the runner.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK LANDED — AND WAS MEASURED. Heartbeats through the plain document path are the slow poison the debate predicted: every Content.upsert_document patch unconditionally inserts 3 rows (full-content revision snapshot + mutation_event + audit) with NO revision GC anywhere — 43k-86k rows/day for a 10-listener fleet at 30s beats, a third of it permanent revision noise. The lean Tasks.Pulse idiom (raw atomic Repo.update_all bypassing Content entirely) mints ZERO revision/audit rows and exactly 1 mutation_event. The charter's lean-write clause is therefore mandatory. Two refinements Decide must pin: (a) Tasks.Pulse is a PATTERN, not a callable — its check_holder gate is claim-lease-specific and would always refuse a listener; the wave needs a sibling module with its own advisory-lock family (listener:<doc_id>), a worker-identity gate, and server-stamped last_seen (all 10 task write modules already stamp DateTime.utc_now() server-side — client clocks never trusted). (b) 'Mints no revision per beat' means no revision ROW; the doc's rev field still bumps (no non-content column exists on documents). Whether even the 1 mutation_event per beat is needed is OPEN — the roster is a pure read with no SSE-tick consumer named; a verifier now enumerates every mutation_events consumer to answer it.

CONTRADICTIONS RESOLVED OR FLAGGED. (i) fleet-orchestrator SKILL.md §6 names Herd report_state as this mechanism's 'native home' — charter PDF-D12 overrules (herd demoted to optional-later; canonical roster = Fleet Card + bp fleet roster; herd-s6 is still an unbuilt open task, so no live migration conflict) and the SKILL.md line gets amended in-wave. (ii) Shared Storm's Barkpark.Pulse doctrine ('presence rows are ephemeral ROWS, not documents — draft logic and webhook fan-out are pure overhead') cuts against 'a listener is just a document'; the lean write path answers the same concern, but Decide must say so explicitly rather than silently disagree with adjacent prior art. (iii) Naming: this wave adds the repo's FOURTH 'fleet' (cloud instance fleet, chat FleetHub, epic_fleet.ex) and fourth 'pulse/presence' — new moduledocs must self-disambiguate exactly the way Tasks.Pulse's own moduledoc already does. (iv) PDF-D2's 'scope is intrinsic via bp use' is only HALF-true: flat token_root mutation routes derive tenancy from the BEARER TOKEN (DeriveWorkspaceFromToken → AssignDefaultScope fallback), not from local bp use config; only the scoped read family threads bp-use context. The heartbeat write and the roster read MUST ride the same scope source or the roster silently reads empty — a verifier settles the mount.

THE ONE HIDDEN GO TRAP IS RENDERING, NOT DISPATCH. renderTable only unwraps list payloads whose envelope key sits on a hardcoded Go allowlist (documents, docs, hits, …). A bespoke {"roster": [...]} envelope degrades to one crammed key/value cell on EVERY installed bp binary until a Go edit + fresh cli-v* release + reinstall propagates — directly undermining 'works on a stranger's machine instantly'. Cheapest honest path: the roster response nests rows under the already-allowlisted documents key (zero Go). Kubectl-style WORKER-first column order needs a cosmetic pickColumns edit; Decide rules whether that is in-wave Go or backlog polish. install-cli.sh's old 404 is fixed and closed — a stranger's first install works today.

FATE-SHARING IS SETTLED AND THE PROOF CAN RUN LOCALLY. PDS-D243/D263 already paid for the sidecar lesson: '& disown' children die or survive depending on WHICH signal kills the parent (ambiguous), and setsid detach is structurally immortal — so the detached-heartbeat ban holds with receipts. The bash runner beats INSIDE its single foreground loop (it currently has NO idle beat at all — pulse only fires mid-order; adding that beat is the wave's runner change, and the single-process shape must be called out as load-bearing, not incidental). The resident skill beats only at turn boundaries (idle-costs-nothing law: an SSE-parked session cannot beat) → honestly longer TTL; NO numeric TTL precedent exists anywhere in Barkpark — Decide picks fresh numbers per form. The kill-a-listener proof runs locally: the mix phx.server OOM does NOT apply to the compiled-release path — scripts/pds-scratch-target.sh boots an isolated instance (own PG + HTTP port, token minted) in ~10-33s WARM, and PDS's negative-control flags are the exact mutation-test pattern (stub status to always-online, assert the harness REDS). Roster status must be computed server-side in ONE module — the repo already carries 3 drifted copies of the same staleness math across two languages — and 'working on task-X' must be a read-time join on claim.worker || assignee (board_live.ex:1013), never a stored status string (lease expiry keeps assignee but frees the claim — a stored copy would lie).

OPERATIONAL HAZARD, PRE-EXISTING BUT BLOCKING: this checkout's main is 8 commits ahead / 136 behind origin/main, and the epic charter file (.claude/workflows/bp-personal-dev-fleet-charter.md) exists ONLY locally — it is not on origin/main. tooling/fleet/ and both fleet skills ARE on origin/main (merged #5178, byte-identical). Builders must work in worktrees cut from origin/main, and the charter must land via a clean PR, or the epic's constitution stays invisible to every other session. A verifier confirms the exact state and hands Decide a steward plan.

Coverage map — what was checked, found, and NOT found

  • FOUND / settled with file:line evidence: manifest dispatch (tree.go, load.go — manifest refetched per invocation, new verbs live instantly); tasks-plugin seams (register_schemas :74, register_routes :403, cli_commands :476, task.pulse map :914); write-path costs (writer.ex → broadcast.ex 3-insert trace; pulse.ex lean idiom); GitHub sync filter (outbox.ex :40-46 literal); SSE listen internals (no connection registry anywhere); kill semantics (PDS-D243/D263 measured); cmux worker-id tiering (4-tier precedence, worth mirroring) and its client-approximate staleness (worth rejecting); herd substrate shape (chat_sessions column + sweeper — PDF-D12 forbids retrofit); tenancy plug chains (DeriveWorkspaceFromToken / AssignDefaultScope vs scoped reads); console path (same-origin Studio, auth_tier read matches all 12 /v1/tasks routes; cloud control plane is the WRONG home — different app, different 'fleet'); TTL/staleness precedents (all three existing systems are write-side reapers — Wave A's read-time-only computation is a deliberate first); scratch-target harness (boot costs measured, teardown clean); fence-bug status (open, Wave D, zero presence coupling); claim-join precedent (board_live.ex:1013); collision sweep (5 open PRs, none touch reserved paths; ~20 'fleet' worktrees are all the OTHER fleets).
  • NOT FOUND — absences that are decisions-in-waiting: no /v1/fleet route, no fleet CLI noun, no listener schema (true greenfield); no server-side SSE connection state ('feed: connected' impossible as a read — would be a self-declared field if ever wanted); no revision GC (plain-patch heartbeats would bloat forever); no read-time-only status precedent server-side; no numeric TTL precedent anywhere; no roster/enumeration surface for any worker kind (bp cmux status is self-report only); no idle heartbeat in fleet-run.sh; epic task has 0 children; no foreign claims on the reserved files.
  • CORNERS NO SURVEYOR REACHED: chrome_table.go's body (90 lines, unread — is it even in the roster's render path?); board_live.ex's own age_label twin (grep came back empty — duplication claim rests on chat_live.ex's comment); the Claude-harness session-kill signal path toward run_in_background children (unknowable from this repo; moot under the no-backgrounding law unless Decide reopens it); Studio-side scope derivation for the console read (assigned to verify); tasks_controller.ex's action-list crowding (roster action placement).

Verify plan — 6 assignments, in flight

  • V1 scratch-live-writecost (OPUS, runs proof): boot scripts/pds-scratch-target.sh on the main checkout's warm _build, prove the release serves and the tasks plugin is live (curl /v1/capabilities + /api/schemas), then prove the write-cost claim at L1: create+claim a task, bp task pulse twice, psql-count revisions/mutation_events/audit_log deltas; patch a doc twice, count again; teardown clean. This proves local proof-harness viability AND pulse-mints-no-revision-row AND plain-patch-mints-3 — the keystone lean-write decision rests on it.
  • V2 cli-envelope-proof (SONNET, worktree, runs Go gate): on a worktree off origin/main run CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... ./internal/manifest/...; add a throwaway probe test proving renderTable yields a real table from a {"documents": [...]} envelope and a crammed cell from {"roster": [...]}; report which envelope GET /v1/tasks index returns today (how does bp task ls get its table?).
